transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-12
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Jamie Carter (Redwood AE), Rohit Malhotra (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (CrestPay), Liam O'Neill (CrestPay), Derek Wu (CrestPay)

Summary (auto):
Redwood walkthrough focused on SDK integration options (Python + TypeScript), auth patterns (API keys, SSO), environment setup and quickstarts. Customer interested in hosted first with potential move to Dedicated. Action items and next steps recorded.

Topics:
- Quickstarts: pip/npm installs, env vars, sample request
- Auth: API key vs SSO/SAML + KMS concerns
- Runtime: batching, KV cache, latency/cost tradeoffs
- Deployment options: Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC)
- POC scope and benchmarking

Transcript:
[00:00] Jamie Carter (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick agenda — we'll run through the python and ts sdks, auth and env setup, then demo a couple of quickstarts and go over next steps. sound good?
[00:15] Maya Chen (CrestPay): yep that works for us, thanks. we're mainly focused on lowering latency for chat flows and keeping costs predictable.
[00:28] Rohit Malhotra (Redwood SE): perfect. i'll jump into the se side — show packages, install, and a live example of streaming and function calls.
[00:45] Liam O'Neill (CrestPay): quick constraints — we need SSO, SOC 2 logs, and data residency in eu-west. also interested in an initial smoke test on hosted before considering dedicated.
[01:02] Jamie Carter (Redwood): noted. we support SSO/SAML for the console and API access control, plus audit logs and region pinning. we'll share our security whitepaper after the call.
[01:20] Derek Wu (CrestPay): also curious: how painful is onboarding for our engs? we have node + python stacks.
[01:33] Rohit Malhotra (Redwood SE): onboarding is usually pretty fast. for python it's pip install redwood-inference, for ts/npm it's @redwood/inference. basic flow is set REDWOOD_API_KEY in env or use service account creds in vault — i'll show both.
[02:05] Rohit: jumping to code — python quickstart. first create a virtualenv, pip install redwood-inference. sample snippet:
    # python example (spoken)
    from redwood import Client
    client = Client(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY'))
    resp = client.chat.create(model='redwood-1', input='summarize this...')
    print(resp.text)
[02:40] (transcription glitch) Speaker 1: they said redwood one, sometimes transcribed as redwood won, but it's the en model version.
[02:55] Maya: are there typed clients for typescript? types/interfaces?
[03:05] Rohit: yes. ts sample:
    import { RedwoodClient } from '@redwood/inference'
    const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY })
    const resp = await client.chat.create({ model: 'redwood-1', input: 'translate...' })
    console.log(resp.output)
[03:40] Jamie: auth patterns — you can use a single api key per team for quickstarts, or short-lived tokens via our SSO integration for prod. if you need encryption at rest with customer-managed keys we integrate with common kms/hsm providers.
[04:05] Liam: for our security team, we'd need to rotate keys automatically and have audit logs. does the api expose token rotation hooks?
[04:20] Rohit: yes you can rotate keys via the console or call our management api. audit logs show request ids, model used, and token-level cost. we also log region and tenant id for compliance.
[04:45] Derek: excellent — about environment setup, what's the recommended pattern for dev vs prod?
[04:55] Rohit: dev: local env var REDWOOD_API_KEY or a .env file (we provide samples). prod: prefer vault / secrets manager + short-lived tokens or the private deployment option if you want a VPC. Quickstarts include a sample docker-compose with the env mounted.
[05:20] Maya: any gotchas on streaming? Our chat UI uses streaming tokens and we need low latency.
[05:35] Rohit: streaming is supported in both sdks. for python we stream via an async iterator, for ts it's an event stream (server-sent events or websocket depending on client). keep in mind batching can slightly increase latency but reduces cost; we can configure per-route latency SLOs.
[06:05] Jamie: also talk about model variants — you can route to cheaper quantized variants for background tasks and use higher-accuracy models for critical flows.
[06:20] Liam: can we pin model versions?
[06:30] Rohit: yes, customers can pin model version and rollout with canaries in the console. that ties into Redwood Optimize where we suggest quantization profiles and batching per workload. note: transcript might show Optimize as Optimizee or Optimizer in some docs but it's the same product.
[07:00] (silence, typing)
[07:20] Rohit: live demo time — i'll show python quickstart running a streaming chat and then a ts example for function calling.
[07:35] Rohit: starting python demo — virtualenv activated, REDWOOD_API_KEY set to the test key (we're on a sandbox account). running sample... response streaming in — partial tokens display in the UI.
[08:05] Maya: that's looking good. can you show the raw http request too?
[08:15] Rohit: sure — behind the sdk it's a POST to /v1/chat with Authorization: Bearer <key>. body contains model, messages, max_tokens, streaming flag. we log request id in response headers for traceability.
[08:45] Jamie: on pricing — hosted is usage-based (per token + embedding unit). Dedicated gives reserved capacity and predictable throughput — we'll send a simple cost comparison for your expected QPS.
[09:05] Liam: what's the rough delta for dedicated vs hosted?
[09:12] Jamie: it depends on throughput; for high steady workloads Dedicated can be 30-50% cheaper at scale because of reserved GPU utilization, but it has commit terms. we'll run numbers based on your 95th percentile QPS.
[09:40] Derek: sample integration question — do we need to modify prompts significantly when switching quantized models?
[09:52] Rohit: typically you don't need major prompt changes; some models may behave slightly differently so we recommend a small eval set. Redwood Optimize can run prompt-level regressions and alert if quality drops.
[10:20] Maya: can you show the quickstart repo link?
[10:25] Jamie: i'll paste links in the chat after the call — python quickstart, ts quickstart, console walkthrough, and security whitepaper.
[10:40] Rohit: switching to TypeScript demo — npm i @redwood/inference, sample env and tsconfig included. here's function call example: you define a schema for the function and the sdk marshals args automatically.
[11:05] (minor crosstalk)
[11:20] Liam: about on-prem — if we went private, what changes? network latency?
[11:30] Rohit: Private (VPC/on-prem) runs a customer-managed control plane and we can run the runtime close to your services to minimize network hop. there is more operational complexity but it's ideal for regulated data. Dedicated is a managed isolated pool if you prefer less ops.
[12:00] Maya: any RBAC for team members? we want least-privilege access per environment.
[12:10] Jamie: yes, console supports role-based access control and you can create service accounts scoped to specific routes/models.
[12:35] Derek: KMS integration — can we bring our key?
[12:45] Rohit: yes, customer-managed keys via kms are supported for encryption at rest. we integrate with common KMS providers (aws kms, gcp kms, azure key vault) and HSM options for higher compliance.
[13:10] Maya: onboarding timeline — how long from sign to running a smoke test?
[13:20] Jamie: with the sandbox it's same-day. production with SSO and audit config can be a few days to a couple weeks depending on compliance gating.
[13:40] Rohit: quick note on logs — our per-route dashboard shows token counts, latencies, cost per token, and request samples (redacted).
[14:00] Maya: great. about SDK versioning — how do we handle breaking changes?
[14:10] Rohit: SDK follows semver; we publish migration guides and major changes come with deprecation windows. also our api is fairly stable but we do recommend pinning to a major version.
[14:45] (15 minute mark check-in)
[15:00] Rohit: moving to more advanced: batching and KV cache. for chat we maintain a KV cache (kv cache) for prefix and reuse across requests to speed up generation. continuous batching groups parallel requests to improve GPU utilization. both are configurable at the route level.
[15:30] Liam: how visible is batching in metrics?
[15:40] Rohit: visible in the console as batch size histogram, avg latency vs token throughput. you can set max_batch_delay to tune latency vs cost.
[16:05] Maya: we have a question about observability retention — how long are traces kept?
[16:15] Jamie: default retention is 30 days, enterprise add-on for extended retention available. we'll include retention options in the security doc.
[16:40] Derek: any limits on embeddings? we plan to build a semantic search for support tickets.
[16:50] Rohit: embeddings are supported, we expose end points for batch embedding and incremental. cost is per-embedding unit; we can recommend quantized models for cheap vectorization at scale.
[17:10] Maya: will the SDK handle batching of embedding requests?
[17:20] Rohit: yes the client has a batch helper but you can also send batched arrays directly to the embedding endpoint.
[17:45] (brief pause)
[18:00] Jamie: let's recap next steps — we'll share quickstarts and security docs, CrestPay will run initial smoke tests, and we'll reconvene for POC scoping.
[18:20] Maya: sounds good. one more: can you share a small benchmark script we can run against hosted to measure 95th percentile p99 lat?
[18:35] Rohit: yes — i'll attach a lightweight benchmark script that calls streaming chat and records p50/p95/p99 latencies; use the sandbox key so it doesn't hit production quotas.
[19:00] Liam: any note about error handling / fallbacks? if a model is slow do we auto-fallback to a smaller variant?
[19:10] Rohit: we support smart routing with fallbacks — you can set policy to fallback to a compatible variant or region if latency degrades. automatic retries and circuit breakers are supported.
[19:45] Derek: ok that's helpful.
[20:00] (wrap up chatter)
[20:20] Jamie: i'll send the links now and follow up with the pricingsheet. last callouts: provisioning sandbox creds, run smoke test, and we'll set up POC scoping with security + infra.
[20:40] Maya: thanks Jamie, Rohit. good session.
[20:50] Rohit: thanks all.
[21:00] (call ends)

Notes on transcription: occasional mislabels (Speaker 1) and model names slighty off, punctuation inconsistent. References shared: quickstart repos (links to be pasted by Jamie), security whitepaper (pdf), benchmark script (attached).

End of transcript.
